blocks.text: 然而根据Anthropic的S-1文件，这些风投公司中没有一家持股达到5%，而5%是列入主要股东名单的门槛。这极不寻常。在典型的科技公司IPO中，领投的风投机构通常在其投资的初创公司中持有两位数的百分比股份。原因在于Anthropic的规模。按其9650亿美元的私募估值计算，1%的股份价值近100亿美元，因此，例如根据近期报道的彭博数据，Menlo约140亿美元的头寸仅占该公司约1.5%。

blocks.text: 尽管这些风投公司可能缺乏可观的百分比持股，但Anthropic向战略合作伙伴——同时也是其业务伙伴的公司——出售了大量股份。事实上，亚马逊很可能是此次IPO最大的单一财务受益者。

blocks.text: 亚马逊于2023年首次投资Anthropic，承诺向这家AI公司投资最多40亿美元。此后，亚马逊又向Anthropic投入了数十亿美元。亚马逊并未预先取得股票，而是将其大部分投资设计为可转换票据，这是一种在IPO或出售时转换为股份的债务。

blocks.text: 根据S-1文件，截至6月30日，亚马逊持有的可转换票据未偿本金为62亿美元。这就是Anthropic的全部债务负担。但随着Anthropic的估值在连续多轮融资中飙升，这些票据将转换成的股份变得价值高得多。亚马逊自己的文件显示，截至6月30日，其持有的票据价值为979亿美元。

blocks.text: 随着亚马逊可转换票据价值飙升，Anthropic不得不在账面上记录其所欠款项不断增长的价值。该公司在利润表上以“可转换票据、衍生负债和SAFE的公允价值变动”项目报告了这些调整，该项目在2026年上半年合计为724亿美元。这笔费用是非现金性质的，意味着公司没有资金流出。

blocks.text: 根据S-1文件，亚马逊的票据最多可转换为18.4亿股。但一项上限将亚马逊限制在Anthropic“部分稀释”股本总数的12%，该数字计入了一些尚未发行的股份，例如股票期权。亚马逊可以放弃该上限。无法转换的票据将继续存续，并在后续季度转换，但受同一限制约束。

blocks.text: 但这些票据只是亚马逊持股的一部分。根据亚马逊截至6月30日的季度报告，该公司第二季度又投资了100亿美元的非投票优先股（一种股权）。亚马逊是通过在Anthropic最近两轮融资中各投资50亿美元做到这一点的。加上2023年至2025年间对票据投资的80亿美元，亚马逊的总投资额约为180亿美元。

blocks.text: 除了股票收益外，亚马逊还将继续从Anthropic获得可观的收入，后者已承诺在未来10年内在AWS上支出至少1100亿美元。

inlines.text: 除了股票收益外，亚马逊还将继续从Anthropic获得可观的收入，后者已承诺在未来10年内在AWS上支出至少1100亿美元。

blocks.text: 谷歌也将从此次上市以及其与 Anthropic 的云计算交易中获得巨额收益。根据法庭文件（《纽约时报》曾对此进行报道），截至去年年初，这家搜索巨头持有 Anthropic 约 14% 的股份，此后又追加了投资，包括 4 月份的 100 亿美元。（谷歌很可能在随后的大规模融资轮次中被稀释，PitchBook 分析师 Harrison Rolfes 告诉 TechCrunch，他估计其目前持股比例更接近 5.6%。）此外，它还从 Anthropic 获得了到 2033 年至少 1140 亿美元的云服务承诺。

blocks.text: Many investors stand to win big when Anthropic goes public. Stakes held by firms including Menlo Ventures, Sequoia, Sound Ventures, and Spark Capital are expected to return billions.

blocks.text: Yet according to Anthropic’s S-1, none of those VC firms owns 5%, the threshold for being included in the principal stockholders’ table. That’s highly unusual. In a typical tech IPO, lead venture investors hold double-digit-percentage stakes in the startups they backed. The reason is Anthropic’s size. At its $965 billion private valuation, a 1% stake is worth nearly $10 billion, so, for example, Menlo’s roughly $14 billion position is only about 1.5% of the company, according to recently reported Bloomberg figures.

blocks.text: While the venture firms may lack sizable percentage stakes, Anthropic sold large stakes to strategic partners, companies that are also its business partners. Indeed, Amazon is likely the single largest financial beneficiary of the IPO.

inlines.text: While the venture firms may lack sizable percentage stakes, Anthropic sold large stakes to strategic partners, companies that are also its business partners. Indeed, Amazon is likely the single largest financial beneficiary of the IPO.

blocks.text: Amazon first backed Anthropic in 2023 with a commitment to invest up to $4 billion in the AI company. Since then, Amazon has poured billions more into Anthropic. Instead of taking stock upfront, Amazon structured much of its investment as convertible notes, a type of debt that converts into shares upon an IPO or sale.

blocks.text: According to the S-1, Amazon holds convertible notes with $6.2 billion in principal outstanding as of June 30. That is Anthropic’s entire debt load. But as Anthropic’s valuation soared across successive funding rounds, the shares those notes will convert into became far more valuable. Amazon’s own filings valued its note holdings at $97.9 billion as of June 30.

blocks.text: As the value of Amazon’s convertible notes surged, Anthropic had to record the growing value of what it owes on its books. It reported the adjustments on its income statement under “change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs,” a line that totaled $72.4 billion for the first half of 2026. The charge is non-cash, meaning no money left the company.

blocks.text: Amazon’s notes could convert into as many as 1.84 billion shares, according to the S-1. But a cap limits Amazon to 12% of Anthropic’s “partially diluted” share count, a figure that counts some shares not yet issued, such as stock options. Amazon can waive the cap. Notes that can’t convert will stay outstanding and convert in later quarters, subject to the same limit.

blocks.text: But the notes are only part of Amazon’s holdings. It further invested $10 billion in nonvoting preferred stock (a type of equity), in the second quarter, according to Amazon’s quarterly report for the period ended June 30. Amazon did this by investing $5 billion in each of Anthropic’s last two funding rounds. Combined with the $8 billion it invested in the notes from 2023 through 2025, that brings Amazon’s total investment to about $18 billion.

blocks.text: Beyond its stock gains, Amazon will also continue to earn significant revenue from Anthropic, which has committed to spend at least $110 billion on AWS over the next 10 years.

blocks.text: Google, too, is set for a major windfall from both the listing and its cloud computing deals with Anthropic. The search giant held about 14% of Anthropic as of early last year, according to court filings that were reported by The New York Times, and has invested more since, including $10 billion in April. (Google was likely diluted in subsequent and massive funding rounds, with PitchBook analyst Harrison Rolfes telling TechCrunch he estimates its current stake at closer to 5.6%.) It has also secured at least $114 billion in cloud commitments from the Anthropic through 2033.

blocks.text: While VCs set for massive paydays have little reason to complain, the S-1 makes it clear that the biggest winners of Anthropic’s IPO may well be tech giants like Amazon, which backed a would-be rival early on and now sell it much of the computing power it runs on.
